title: Müsait bir yerde!
goal: Choose between spoken and standard spelling for each reader, get around by dolmuş, and follow a scene that mixes standard narration with spoken dialogue.

intro.text: Standard spelling is always correct; spoken spelling is a choice. Write *geliyo*, *gelicem* and *kanka* to friends, and keep them out of emails, forms and anything for work or school. In a dolmuş you'll hear the street version of Turkish: *İnecek var!*, *Arkadan iki tam!*, *Müsait bir yerde!*

vocab.en: minibus (larger than a dolmuş, on a fixed route)
line, route (of a bus or a dolmuş) (accusative: hattı)
transfer, change (between lines) (aktarma yapmak: to change)
One full fare, one student fare.
Wherever it's convenient! (asking the driver to stop)
to drop off (a passenger); to lower, to take down; to download

exercises.question: Where would *Geliyom, bi dakka!* be fine in writing?
options: a text message to a friend

why.1: A cover letter is formal: *Geliyorum, bir dakika* wouldn't belong there either.
why.2: To a professor, write the standard: *geliyorum*, *bir dakika*.
why.3: Anything for work keeps to the standard.

exercises.explain: Spoken spelling belongs in messages to friends and family, and in dialogue.

accept: geleceksin

reject.why: Spoken: the ending shrinks in questions. In standard Turkish: *geleceksin*.

exercises.hint: Your friend texted *Saat kaçta gelcen?* Write it in standard spelling.
exercises.explain: *Gelcen* is the fast spoken *geleceksin*: the vowel of `-(y)AcAk` and most of *-sin* disappear.

exercises.prompt: Şoför bey, müsait bir yerde inebilir miyim?
accept: Driver, can I get off somewhere convenient?
Excuse me, driver, [can|could|may] I get off [somewhere convenient|at a convenient place|at a convenient spot|wherever it is convenient|when it is convenient]?
Driver, can I get off at a convenient place?
Driver, can I get off at a convenient spot?
Driver, can I get off wherever it is convenient?
Driver, can I get off when it is convenient?
Driver, could I get off [somewhere convenient|at a convenient place|at a convenient spot|wherever it is convenient|when it is convenient]?
Driver, may I get off [somewhere convenient|at a convenient place|at a convenient spot|wherever it is convenient|when it is convenient]?
Driver, [can|could] you let me [off|out] [somewhere convenient|at a convenient place|at a convenient spot|wherever it is convenient]?
[Excuse me|Sir], [can|could|may] I get off [somewhere convenient|at a convenient place|at a convenient spot|wherever it is convenient]?
exercises.explain: *Şoför bey* is the polite way to address a driver; *müsait bir yerde* (at a suitable place) leaves it to him to choose where to stop.

exercises.question: In a dolmuş, someone behind you taps your shoulder, hands you some money and says *Bir tam!* What do you do?
options: Pass it forward to the driver

why.1: The money is a fare: *bir tam*, one full fare.
why.2: The passenger isn't returning anything: the money is for the driver.
why.3: Nobody is asking you to get off.

exercises.explain: In a dolmuş, fares travel hand to hand to the driver, and the change comes back the same way.

accept: İnecek var!
Müsait bir yerde inecek var!
İnecek var, şoför bey!
Şoför bey, inecek var!
İnen var!
exercises.explain: *İnecek var* (there is someone who will get off) is the set phrase; *müsait bir yerde* can come in front.

exercises.en: Two full fares from the back!
exercises.explain: *Tam* is a full fare, *öğrenci* a student fare: *Arkadan iki tam!*, *Bir tam, bir öğrenci!*

exercises.title: Dolmuşta yirmi dakika
exercises.passage:
Akşam saat altıydı. Dolmuş durağında uzun bir kuyruk vardı. Sıram gelince arka koltuğa oturdum; dolmuş dolar dolmaz şoför yola çıktı.

Biraz sonra arkamdaki genç omzuma dokundu ve bana para uzattı:

— Abla, bi zahmet öne uzatır mısın? İki tam.

Parayı öndeki yolcuya verdim, o da şoföre. Bir dakika sonra para üstü aynı yoldan geri geldi.

Yanımdaki teyze telefonla konuşuyordu:

— Geliyom kızım, geliyom! Trafik var, yarım saate oradayım. Sen sofrayı kur, ben gelicem.

Yolun sonuna yaklaşınca genç yine seslendi:

— Şoför bey, müsait bir yerde inecek var!

Dolmuş kaldırıma yanaştı, genç teşekkür edip indi. Ben de birkaç durak sonra indim. Kimse kimseyi tanımıyordu, ama yirmi dakika boyunca küçük bir aile gibiydik.

glossary.en: to pull in, to pull over

exercises.translation: It was six in the evening. There was a long queue at the dolmuş stop. When my turn came I sat in the back seat; as soon as the dolmuş was full, the driver set off. A little later the young man behind me touched my shoulder and held out some money: “Would you mind passing this forward? Two full fares.” I gave the money to the passenger in front, and he gave it to the driver. A minute later the change came back the same way. The aunt next to me was on the phone: “I'm coming, dear, I'm coming! There's traffic, I'll be there in half an hour. You set the table, I'll be there.” As we neared the end of the route, the young man called out again: “Driver, someone's getting off wherever it's convenient!” The dolmuş pulled in to the kerb; the young man thanked him and got off. I got off a few stops later. Nobody knew anybody, but for twenty minutes we had been like a little family.

questions.q: What does the young man ask the narrator to do?
questions.explain: *Bi zahmet öne uzatır mısın? İki tam.* He hands her the fare for two.

questions.q: How does the change get back to him?
options: The same way, hand to hand
The driver stops and brings it

questions.q: Why does the narration write *konuşuyordu* in full, while the aunt says *Geliyom* and *gelicem*?
options: The narration keeps the standard; the dialogue keeps her voice
The narrator is quoting a formal letter
questions.explain: As in novels, the narration is standard and the dialogue sounds like speech.

exercises.question: Which of these is a spelling mistake, even in a casual message?

why.1: Correct: *dA* written apart. *Geliyom* is spoken spelling, fine in a message.
why.2: Correct: the question particle is written apart, even after a spoken form.
why.3: Spoken spelling, fine in a message to a friend.

exercises.explain: *Bende* means **on me, with me**. **Me too** is *ben de*, with the conjunction written apart, in any register.

accept: Could you pass the change to the back?
Could you pass the change back?
Could you pass the change to the people at the back?
Could you pass the change to the person at the back?
Could you pass the change to the person behind you?
Could you please pass the change [to the back|back|to the people at the back|to the person at the back|to the person behind you]?
Can you (please) pass the change [to the back|back|to the people at the back|to the person at the back|to the person behind you]?
Would you (please) pass the change [to the back|back|to the people at the back|to the person at the back|to the person behind you]?
[Could|Can|Would] you (please) hand the change [back|to the back]?
exercises.explain: *Para üstü* is the change; *arkaya uzatmak* is to hand it back, in the same chain as the fare.

exercises.task: You meant to send this voice message to a friend, but it went to your teacher. Rewrite it as a short, polite email to her: standard spelling, *siz*, no informal words, a greeting and a closing.
exercises.source: Hocam slm, bi sorun var: otobüs gelmiyo, derse geç kalıcam herhâlde. Ödevi de bitirmedim valla, yarın getircem. Tmm mı?
models: Merhaba Hocam, otobüs gecikiyor; bu yüzden derse birkaç dakika geç kalacağım. Ayrıca ödevimi henüz bitiremedim; izin verirseniz yarın getirmek istiyorum. Anlayışınız için teşekkür ederim. Saygılarımla, Deniz
Sayın Hocam, otobüs henüz gelmediği için derse geç kalabilirim, kusura bakmayın. Ödevimi de tamamlayamadım; uygun görürseniz yarın teslim edeceğim. Teşekkür ederim. İyi çalışmalar, Deniz
checklist: No *slm*, *bi*, *valla* or *tmm*; a greeting and a closing instead
A polite softener for the request: *izin verirseniz*, *uygun görürseniz*

exercises.en: Can I get off somewhere convenient?
